title: PEB Accessories: Skylights, Vents, Doors | Steel Mind Engineers
description: Skylights, ventilators, louvers, insulation, doors, ladders and walkways for pre-engineered buildings. Choose the accessories your building needs.
h1: Accessories for Pre-Engineered Buildings: Light, Air, Insulation, Doors and Safe Access
quickAnswer: PEB accessories control light, air, temperature, entry and safe access. They include skylights, ventilators, louvers, insulation, doors, ladders, stairs and walkways, and they are chosen by the use of the building.
alt: Skylights and ridge ventilator on the roof of a steel building; insulated door; cage ladder on a steel wall.

faq.q: Do skylights make the building hot?
faq.a: Quality translucent sheets give light with less heat. The engineer will advise on the right quantity.

faq.q: Can accessories be added after handover?
faq.a: Yes. Many can be fitted later if the frame is ready for them.

blocks.text: The frame and the sheets make a building. The accessories make it comfortable, safe and usable. Steel Mind Engineers supplies and fits them with the building, so each item is ordered at the right stage and carries the same finish as the rest of the structure.

items.name: Rockwool insulation board
items.text: A dense mineral-wool board that insulates roofs and walls against heat and noise. It resists fire and moisture.

items.name: Fiberglass insulation
items.text: A light blanket laid under roof sheets or inside wall panels to reduce heat transfer and sound. It is easy to install.

items.name: Skylight
items.text: Translucent roof panels that bring daylight inside and cut daytime electricity use.

items.name: Ridge ventilator
items.text: A continuous vent along the ridge that lets rising hot air and moisture leave without power.

items.name: Turbo vent
items.text: A wind-driven rotating ventilator on the roof. It removes heat, moisture and fumes without electricity.

items.name: Power ventilator
items.text: A motor-driven roof fan that pushes out hot, stale air and draws in fresh air in large enclosed spaces.

items.name: Louver
items.text: A set of slats in a wall opening that lets air pass while keeping out rain and sun. It is useful in poultry and dairy sheds.

items.name: Double sliding door
items.text: A large door that opens along a track beside the wall. It saves floor space and gives a wide opening for vehicles.

items.name: Hangar door
items.text: A very large door for aircraft, vehicles or oversized equipment that leaves the floor clear when open.

items.name: PU-filled door
items.text: A door with a polyurethane foam core. It insulates against heat and sound and resists moisture, which suits cold rooms.

items.name: Sectional motorized roll-up door
items.text: An insulated door made of horizontal panels that rise overhead on a motor. It suits loading bays.

items.name: Emergency exit door
items.text: A fire-resistant door with panic hardware that opens quickly under pressure to give a clear escape route.

items.name: Cage ladder
items.text: A fixed vertical ladder enclosed by a safety cage, with anti-slip rungs, for roofs and elevated platforms.

items.name: Staircase
items.text: A steel stair with correct tread, riser and handrails for floors, platforms and roofs.

items.name: Walkway
items.text: A slip-resistant steel pathway with handrails that connects floors, mezzanines and equipment.

blocks.text: Pick accessories by use. A poultry shed needs ventilation first. A warehouse needs skylights and dock doors. A workshop needs light and fume control. The engineer will advise during the design stage, and many accessories can also be fitted after handover if the frame is ready for them.
